candidate.diagnosis: The latest paired development evaluation retained full native success (4/4 in each arm) but used 16 decisions in both arms, so it did not pass the efficiency gate. Spatial improved from 2 to 1 decisions (72 to 73 ticks), and Goal from 3 to 1 (111 to 115 ticks), with actual program execution in both successful candidate instances. Object worsened from 4 to 5 decisions (133 to 141 ticks), and Long from 7 to 9 (269 to 356 ticks), canceling those savings. Object's candidate issued the identical complete instruction five times and nevertheless reached native success; this supplies new evidence for batching that continuation, not evidence of an already validated Object program. There is no infrastructure failure to repair and no demonstrated tick-efficiency improvement.
candidate.hypothesis: ONE change: extend initial caller-side routing of the existing bounded full-goal program to the observed single-object alphabet-soup-to-basket task. Retain Spatial and drawer routing, retain the implementation, and leave Long orchestration unchanged. The Object candidate's five unchanged-instruction decisions suggest avoidable GPT overhead; batching may preserve native success while eliminating intervening decisions. Predict no full-task success regressions and more than 10% fewer aggregate GPT decisions at equal positive success in fresh paired validation. This prediction is untested. Object previously used shorter final calls, and uninterrupted delegation can delay corrective intervention; its successful direct-call trajectory does not guarantee successful program execution. Any success regression or failure of the frozen promotion gate rejects the proposal.

memory.lesson: Spatial and Goal both reached native success through the program, reducing decisions from 2 to 1 and 3 to 1 respectively, with slightly more ticks. Preserve these routes; these two development instances do not establish general mastery.
memory.title: Retain measured delegation benefits

memory.lesson: Object succeeded at 133 baseline ticks and 141 candidate ticks. The candidate repeated the exact full goal across five decisions without executing the program. Test batching this repetition; neither reduced motion cost nor Object program transfer has been demonstrated.
memory.title: Object now has direct continuation evidence

memory.lesson: Long remained successful but worsened from 7 decisions/269 ticks to 9/356. Overall decisions stayed at 16 despite two successful program instances. Do not claim promotion, extrapolate to Long, or count successful primitive execution as original-task completion.
memory.title: Aggregate retention is not aggregate improvement

program.description: Unchanged bounded delegation implementation; the only intervention is adding the observed Object task to caller-side initial routing alongside Spatial and drawer opening. args has only instruction, supplied as the exact complete original goal. Two nonnested literal-range loops provide two primitive call sites, at most eight invocations and 320 control ticks, within the 321-tick operator limit; runtime enforces the 600-second limit. VLA reobserves between chunks. Native terminal success interrupts execution automatically. Any primitive failure is propagated before further motion. Exhaustion returns control without asserting task success and does not itself end the episode. No evaluator query, scene constants, manual gripper intervention, or grasp inference.
program.name: program_bounded_full_goal_delegation

skill.name: Evidence-gated full-goal continuation batching
skill.procedure: 1. Require episode evidence that a complete goal can be successfully continued without GPT instruction changes; do not infer transfer from primitive status. For this candidate, permit initial routing on the observed Spatial bowl placement, middle-drawer opening, and single-object soup placement only. 2. Invoke the program once with the exact original instruction, preserving all object disambiguation and destination requirements. 3. Allow VLA chunk-level reobservation and runtime native-success interruption; never substitute program return status for task success. 4. On primitive failure, inspect current observations and diagnose before any further motion. On cap exhaustion, resume the existing GPT policy within the remaining episode budget rather than automatically repeating the program. 5. Keep Long orchestration unchanged. Validate complete episodes first, then decision cost, and record actual program execution in successful fresh instances.
skill.when_to_use: When in-domain evidence shows repeated full-goal VLA continuation can succeed and intermediate GPT decisions largely repeat that goal. Routing expansion remains a falsifiable experiment; it is not a universal delegation policy.

candidate.task_rationale: Validate existing tasks under the unchanged external protocol: task 0 in Spatial, Object, Goal and Long, four fresh validation resets and separate final resets, with both GPT arms limited to 24 decisions/960 ticks. Do not select cases, modify goals or budgets, or create harder scenes. Only Object's initial program route changes relative to the evaluated predecessor. Score full original-task native success before efficiency. Promotion requires no regressions and increased success or more than 10% fewer decisions at equal positive success, plus actual program execution in two successful fresh instances. The latest predecessor met retention and the program-instance count but not aggregate efficiency; those past instances are not new candidate validation. Infrastructure errors, scoring fixes, and shorter failed attempts cannot count as improvement. This candidate remains untested until fresh paired validation; held-out results are unopened and unavailable, and development success does not establish statistical mastery.

PROCEDURE.md.source:
# Evidence-gated full-goal continuation batching

When in-domain evidence shows repeated full-goal VLA continuation can succeed and intermediate GPT decisions largely repeat that goal. Routing expansion remains a falsifiable experiment; it is not a universal delegation policy.

1. Require episode evidence that a complete goal can be successfully continued without GPT instruction changes; do not infer transfer from primitive status. For this candidate, permit initial routing on the observed Spatial bowl placement, middle-drawer opening, and single-object soup placement only. 2. Invoke the program once with the exact original instruction, preserving all object disambiguation and destination requirements. 3. Allow VLA chunk-level reobservation and runtime native-success interruption; never substitute program return status for task success. 4. On primitive failure, inspect current observations and diagnose before any further motion. On cap exhaustion, resume the existing GPT policy within the remaining episode budget rather than automatically repeating the program. 5. Keep Long orchestration unchanged. Validate complete episodes first, then decision cost, and record actual program execution in successful fresh instances.

proposal.diagnosis: On these eight seed-0 development tasks, checkpoint-only achieves native success on 7/8; GPT policy on 6/8. The clearest repair targets are discovery/libero_goal-00-s0--gpt_policy (drawer: failed after 21 GPT decisions, 793 ticks) versus its checkpoint_only pair (success at 133 ticks), and discovery/libero_10-01-s0--gpt_policy (both dairy items: declared completed at 260 ticks without native success) versus its checkpoint_only pair (success at 237 ticks). Repeated instruction rewriting and premature completion are plausible orchestration problems, not proven causal explanations. Successful primitive execution does not establish task completion. Universal checkpoint substitution is unsupported: discovery/libero_object-00-s0--checkpoint_only fails at 960 ticks while its GPT pair succeeds at 131 ticks.
proposal.hypothesis: One repair: for the original drawer and two-dairy tasks, replace GPT's repeated rewrites and completion decisions with bounded delegation of the unchanged full original instruction. Up to eight 40-tick VLA segments should recover native success within 320 ticks using one dispatch decision, without manual grasp/release assumptions. This is untested. Falsify the repair if fresh paired trials fail to improve native success on the two targets or lose any paired baseline success. Reduced decisions count as an improvement only after success is preserved; merely hitting the shorter cap does not.

program.description: Caller supplies exactly the full original instruction. Two sequential, nonnested four-iteration loops execute at most eight run_vla calls: two primitive call sites, 320 control ticks, under the runtime's 321-tick/600-second limits. VLA still reobserves between chunks. Native success stops execution externally, including inside calls; the tool never queries the evaluator or infers a grasp. Any primitive failure stops further motion. If execution reaches the final return, the bounded attempt is unsuccessful, not a completion claim. Initially deploy only on the drawer and two-dairy repair targets, with routing outside this generic source.
program.name: bounded_full_goal_delegation

skill.name: Bounded full-goal delegation before semantic intervention
skill.procedure: 1. At episode start, pass the exact original instruction, retaining all objects and relations. 2. Run the bounded delegation tool without intermediate GPT paraphrases or manual release actions. 3. Let the frozen native terminal monitor stop all motion on success. 4. Propagate primitive failure immediately; if the cap is reached, record an unsuccessful attempt, not completion or an efficiency gain. 5. Compare fresh paired full-task outcomes before extending this routing to any other existing task.
skill.when_to_use: Initially test on the original drawer and two-dairy tasks, where matched checkpoint-only episodes succeeded and GPT orchestration failed. More generally, consider this procedure only when unchanged full-goal delegation has supporting development evidence; do not assume it works for single-soup placement.

proposal.task_rationale: Validate existing tasks; no harder tasks or scene creation. Run five fresh paired repetitions from each of the eight supplied original initial states, pairing randomness where supported and keeping checkpoint, sensors, evaluator, and baseline episode budgets fixed. Change only routing for the drawer and two-dairy targets; retain the other six GPT policies, especially single soup. Compare frozen native full-task success first, then GPT calls/tokens, control ticks, and wall time on successful pairs. Require all original tasks to succeed across this validation set, recovery of the two target failures, and no baseline-success/candidate-failure pair before adoption; otherwise original scope remains unmastered. Report cap failures and infrastructure failures separately, without crediting shorter failures, scoring changes, or runtime outages as improvement. These are development tests, not held-out results.
